A pair of your bodyguards step forward, carrying the sample case between them.

They place the container on the hangar floor and without rush or flourish unlatch the cover and withdraw it to reveal the false relic, the upthrust work-glove which was never touched by Ludd.

Oak turns his head ever so slightly. "Destroy it," he rumbles.

The clerk mutters into her cuff.

Oak is content to remain silent as technicians of the Knights wheel out a heavy crucible of sorts, festooned with tubes and patterned heat-dispersal tiles. They halt it several meters from you, then scurry over to retrieve the glove - still in its open sample case - and place the whole lot carefully into the blackened interior. They slowly lower and then seal the heavy top-cover then adjust some knobs and switches. The lead tech looks to the Excubitor Orbis.

He gives a tiny nod.

A dull roar sounds from the device, like a torrential waterfall behind a hardened airlock. Indentations in the tiled carapace begin to glow; you can feel the radiated heat on your exposed skin.

The clerk shuffles nervously, flipping open a notebook, pausing a moment, then flipping it closed. She looks at the Excubitor Orbis.

He nods at her, then looks back to you.

The clerk clears her throat.

"Excubitor Orbis," her eyes dart at you and Bornanew. "$playerSirOrMadam. Novice."

"There is a matter of the Demarch of Olinadu. A Menes Yaribay? He claims he was promised payments for the, um, purchase of a relic."

You hadn't thought Oak could look any more displeased.

The clerk coughs, "We, ah," she flips a page on a paper notebook.

"While the Church does not recognize the purchase of,  um," her eyes flicker to the crucible, which has stopped glowing, but ticks away as it cools. "The object in question. However, due to the promise made by a... representative," she looks quickly at Bornanew, then away. "It was proposed that a... polite settlement with Mister Yaribay be made using the reward credits originally authorized by the Reverend Archcurate Jaspis..."

"Do it," says the Excubitor Orbis.

You can't quite see if Bornanew is blushing, because his head is bowed toward Oak.

The clerk coughs, "We, ah," she flips a page on a paper notebook.

"While the Church does not recognize the purchase of,  um," her eyes flicker to the crucible, which has stopped glowing, but ticks away as it cools. "The object in question. However, due to the promise made by a... representative," she looks quickly at Bornanew, then away. "It was proposed that a... polite settlement with Mister Yaribay be made using the reward credits originally authorized by the Reverend Archcurate Jaspis..."

"Do it," says the Excubitor Orbis.

The clerk clears her throat.

"Excubitor Orbis," her eyes dart at you and Bornanew. "$playerSirOrMadam. Novice."

"There is a matter of the Demarch of Olinadu. A Menes Yaribay? He claims damages from an... incident. He claims that a valuable object was stolen during a violent raid on his personal compound. And, um, there is a list of potential suspects..."

You hadn't thought Oak could look any more displeased.

The clerk coughs, "We, ah," she flips a page on a paper notebook.

"While the Church does not recognize the legitimacy of, um," her eyes flicker to the crucible, which has stopped glowing, but ticks away as it cools. "The object in question. It was proposed that a... polite settlement of affairs with Mister Yaribay be made using the reward credits originally authorized by the Reverend Archcurate Jaspis for..."

"Do it," says the Excubitor Orbis.

You can't quite see if Bornanew is blushing, because his head is bowed toward Oak.

"I t-think that's everything," the clerk says, looking between you and Oak.

Excubitor Orbis Gideon Oak exhales, meeting your gaze. Then, without a word, he turns away and begins walking back to the far doorway casting its long wedge of light into the armored hangar.

After a respectful pause, the clerk and guards rush to follow.

Oak ignores you.

"The novice still wears a crown of pride," Oak says toward Bornanew. "Still he has much to repent."

Bornanew turns slightly aside, keeping his eyes toward the Excubitor Orbis. "I shall be staying here a while, I think," he says softly.

Oak ignores you.

"The novice still wears a crown of pride," Oak says toward Bornanew. "Still he has much to repent."

Bornanew's look hardens. He matches the remorseless gaze of the Excubitor Orbis with his own. "If it be so by Providence," he says.

"No," says Oak. "The novice still wears a crown of pride. He has much to repent."

Bornanew turns aside and says quietly to you, "I shall be staying here a while, I think."

"No," says Oak. "The novice still wears a crown of pride. He has much to repent."

Bornanew does not turn aside from Gideon Oak, matching his remorseless look with his own. "The Excubitor Orbis believes there is much sin for which I must pay. I shall be staying here, as it pleases him."

Oak, for his part, looks very much less than pleased at Bornanew's commentary. His clerk looks mortified.

"Yes," says Bornanew, still caught in a staring-contest with Oak. "You are. I shall be staying here a while, I think."

The world's smallest smile makes a new crease on the Excubitor Orbis' face as he turns to you.

"Novice Bornanew owes you much. But still he wears a crown of pride. Still he must repent."

"But I have a feeling that our paths shall cross again," $global.jethroName says, pulling his simple bundle of possessions onto his shoulder.

Bornanew follows his fellow Knights to the doorway casting its long wedge of light into the armored hangar.

"Our paths shall cross again," $global.jethroName says, eyes in shadow. He pulls his simple bundle of possessions onto his shoulder. "Hammer in one hand, sword in the other."

Oak, ever displeased, turns his back without further comment and begins marching to the far end of the hangar. After a moment, the other Knights, and Bornanew, follow.

They shrink to silhouettes in the long wedge of light cast into the armored hangar, then disappear.

Bornanew, limping slightly, follows his fellow Knights to the doorway casting its long wedge of light into the armored hangar.

Oak, ever displeased, turns his back without further comment and begins marching to the far end of the hangar. After a moment, the other Knights, and Bornanew - limping slightly - follow.

They shrink to silhouettes in the long wedge of light cast into the armored hangar, then disappear.

Your shuttle returns you to your $shipOrFleet.

A ping from your TriPad indicates a funds transfer.

She holds up a hand to stop you from speaking further.

"My trust, and my prayers, are with Jethro. He will do what need be done, and if he trusts you, then I pray that you honor him."

Your $shipOrFleet gets within range of the $nameInText that you've been contracted to run a black-box sensor package on.

However, a hostile fleet is tracking your movements, leaving you no time to stop and run the sensor package.
Your $shipOrFleet gets within range of the $nameInText that you've been contracted to run a black-box sensor package on.

You tap a button to execute the black-box sensor package and wait for it to finish. On completion, it provides an escrow key that authorizes the agreed-upon payment to be transferred to your account.

Presumably, it will transmit the scan results on a secure channel when you're near a comm relay, and then delete itself from your systems.
It's the planet you've been contracted to run a full survey on.

"Well," $Rank $personLastName looks at you for a long moment. "That might be difficult."

"Due to the fact that you hold primary executive authority over a polity which itself holds a form of membership status in the Persean League, you cannot resign your commission until that status is revoked. In fact," $heOrShe twitches subtly, apparently performing an infonet query, "It would be illegal, barring certain extreme conditions."
"Is this some kind of joke? If you are who you say you are, you're on several $faction wanted lists."
"You're already commissioned by $theOtherCommissionFaction. You'll have to resign that commission before you can be commissioned by $theFaction."
"I'm sorry, but you don't meet our criteria for receiving a commission."

"Hmm, yes, you're a suitable candidate.

Accepting a commission is a serious matter. You will be required to fight enemies of $theFaction, wherever they may be found.

You'll be able to resign your commission at any time, though I don't imagine doing so would win you any friends."
"So, how about it? Still want to sign on?"
"Excellent! Welcome to the service."
"Anything else I can do for you?"

"Yes, not everyone has it in them to uphold the values of $theFaction to such a high standard. No shame in it.

Anything else I can do for you?"
"Are you sure? $TheFaction needs people it can rely on, and turning your back like this won't be easily forgotten."
"I can see there's no changing your mind. Well, at least you had the courtesy to tender your resignation in person."
"A good decision. We can use people like you."
"Is this some kind of joke? If you are truly whom you claim to be, you've been condemned in multiple writs by the Most Holy Presbyteriat."
"You're already commissioned by $theOtherCommissionFaction. The heart holds but one faith; until you resign that commission, it would be quite unthinkable to be commissioned by the Church."
"I am sorry, but you are not worthy of receiving a commission from the Church."

"Hmm, yes, you have proven your faith through good works.

Accepting a commission is a serious matter. You will be required to fight enemies of the Church wherever they may be found; to uphold the Eleven Virtues; to condemn and abhor vice.

Your commission may be resigned at any time, though it would be a very poor sign of faith in the Church. And in terms of worldly matters, it would be considered a black mark indeed by Ludd's faithful."
"Will you accept this righteous mantle with the blessings of Ludd?"
"Praise be to the spirit of the stars! I am blessed to be the first to welcome you to this righteous service."
"I shall not detain you from your holy work, but please do not hesitate to ask if there is anything I can do for you."
